slice: KTM-family off-road four-strokes 2020-2026 (KTM 250/350/450 XC-F, 450 XCF-W; Husqvarna FX 350/450, FE 450; GasGas EX 250F/350F/450F, EC 450F) - differences from SX-F/FC/MC, generations, dynos, electronics, setups, issues

records.topic: how the XC-F differs from the SX-F
records.statement: The XC-F cross-country bikes use the SX-F motocross engine, frame and electronics but add an 18-inch rear wheel, a bigger fuel tank (2.25 vs 1.9 gal), a kickstand, skid plate, handguards and an O-ring chain, and from 2024 a spring fork instead of the SX-F air fork. Motor, mapping, exhaust and sound level are the same as the SX-F per this test.

values.fork_2024_on: WP XACT closed-cartridge spring (SX-F: XACT air)

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: Riding the 2025 KTM 450XC-F (The Wrap)

records.notes: Magazine reporting of KTM spec. 'Unchanged' list (motor, mapping, gear ratios, exhaust, sound, 13-51 gearing) is stated relative to the SX-F for the 450; for 250/350 the XC-F has a 6-speed gearbox instead of the SX-F 5-speed (see drivetrain records).

records.statement: The 2020-2022 XC-F bikes share the 2019-generation SX-F frame and engines and use the WP XACT air fork (310 mm / 12.2 in travel). 2020 changes were limited to new fork and shock settings, a new fork piston and a new shock compression adjuster. The 2020 350 XC-F listed at $10,499 with a claimed 222 lb dry weight.

source.name: Dirt Rider buyer's guide: 2020 KTM 350 XC-F

records.notes: Buyer's guide reprint of KTM data. Generation boundary (2019-2022) from 2023 new-generation coverage.

records.statement: For 2023 the XC-F moved to the new SX-F platform: new cylinder head and crankcases, engine tilted back 2 degrees with the countershaft sprocket 3 mm lower, a die-cast swingarm 190 g lighter, a 22 mm rear axle (old 25 mm wheels will not fit), a 15 mm shorter WP XACT shock, a polyamide/aluminium subframe, a new fuel pump that empties the tank further and compact switches with map, traction control and quickshift buttons. It kept the XACT air fork. The 450 XC-F was $11,649 and weighed 246 lb wet on the magazine scale, 6 lb more than before.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2023 KTM 450 XC-F Technical Information

records.notes: Weight is Dirt Rider measured; most other items are KTM press data reported by Dirt Rider.

records.statement: For 2024 every XC-F got a WP XACT closed-cartridge spring fork in place of the air fork, with a hydro-stop in the last 68 mm and a new mid-valve piston; travel dropped 10 mm to 300 mm. A clutchless upshift quickshifter became standard (2nd-5th on the 450, 2nd-6th on the 250/350), and 2023 six-speed owners can add it with a software update.

source.name: Motocross Action: First Look 2024 KTM off-road models

records.notes: KTM press info via MXA first look; travel change and QS ranges confirmed by Ultimate Motorcycling first look. One Cycle News 2025 article also lists the spring fork as replacing the air fork, which reads as a repeat of the 2024 change.

records.statement: 2025 XC-F bikes got the frame first used on the 2024.5 Factory Edition SX-F (cut-outs and changed wall thickness at the head tube, engine mount and shock mount, about 300 g lighter and more flexible), a swingarm with a machined chain slider, linkage with smaller bolts and new seals, new fork and shock settings, a stiffer one-piece air inlet sleeve and snorkel, bi-composite shrouds and a stronger rear brake pedal. The Connectivity Unit Offroad became an optional kit. 450 XC-F MSRP $12,199.

source.name: Racer X: KTM touts advancements for 2025 XC cross-country bikes

records.notes: KTM press data via Racer X; MSRP from Dirt Bike Magazine 2025 test.

records.statement: For 2026 KTM sold only the 250 XC-F and 450 XC-F as standard four-stroke XC models; the 350 XC-F came only as a Factory Edition. Shared updates were a threaded radiator cap, a protective cap on the fuel-line connector, Dunlop AT82 tyres and new graphics; the XC tank is listed at 9 L (2.37 gal).

source.name: Enduro21: First look 2026 KTM XC off-road line-up

records.notes: KTM press data via Enduro21; Dirt Bike Test 2026 first look confirms no standard 350 XC-F and the same small changes.

records.statement: The 2026 350 XC-F Factory Edition ($13,549) adds an FMF muffler, factory triple clamps, wheels, seat and skid plate, a start device, semi-floating front disc, Hinson clutch cover and a standard Connectivity Unit Offroad with GPS sensor, on top of the XC-F spring fork and six-speed Pankl gearbox.

source.name: RideApart: KTM 2026 350 XC-F Factory Edition

records.notes: KTM press data via RideApart. A 2023 350 XC-F Factory Edition also existed (Dirt Rider tech page, details not rendered).

records.statement: The 450 XCF-W returned for 2023 as an off-road competition model replacing the emissions-limited 500 XCF-W. Compared with the EXC-F it has no reed valve in the intake boot, no evaporative system, a more open exhaust and its own map. It kept the older (pre-2023) frame with a WP XPLOR coil fork and linkless PDS shock, and cost $11,649.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2023 KTM 450XCF-W Full Test

records.notes: Cycle News 2023 range announcement also describes it as an 'uncorked' version with improved airflow, no airbox reed system, more open exhaust and unique map. Imported as closed-course; not marketed as dual-sport.

records.statement: For 2024 the 450 XCF-W moved to the new-generation chassis and engine (frame, polyamide subframe and swingarm new, engine tilted 2 degrees back, sprocket 3 mm lower). It got a WP XACT closed-cartridge spring fork (300 mm) and a new WP XPLOR PDS shock (310 mm), a 6-speed wide-ratio gearbox, a 42 mm throttle body and an LED headlight about 300% brighter. KTM claims 107.4 kg without fuel; MSRP $11,999.

source.name: Cycle News: New 2024 KTM 450 XCF-W Four-Stroke Model Specs

records.notes: MSRP from Ultimate Motorcycling 2024 review.

records.statement: 2025 brought a revised swingarm and new XPLOR shock settings ($12,149). For 2026 the fork got shorter, lighter main springs (about 200 g lighter overall), a new pressure reservoir and a one-piece hydrostop, with shock settings revised to match, plus a strapless headlight mask, a threaded radiator cap and a firmer tank mount.

source.name: KTM USA 2026 450 XCF-W model page

records.notes: 2025 details from Cycle World buyer's guide; 2026 from KTM US model page.

records.statement: The 2023 Husqvarna FX 350 and FX 450 moved to the new FC platform with the same changes as KTM (die-cast swingarm 0.4 lb lighter, 22 mm axle, hybrid subframe). The FX 450 has a 5-speed with standard quickshift and still used the XACT air fork in 2023. It weighed 243 lb wet on the magazine scale and listed at $11,649.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2023 Husqvarna FX 450 Technical Information

records.notes: Weight measured by Dirt Rider; other items are Husqvarna data.

records.statement: For 2024 the FX bikes got the WP XACT closed-cartridge spring fork and the FX 350 gained a standard quickshifter (2023 FX 350 owners can add it by software update). For 2025 they got the more flexible frame and Brembo brakes returned; the FX 350 was $12,049. The FX keeps the FC engine, mapping and exhaust and has a lower seat height than the KTM.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2025 Husqvarna FX350 Full Test

records.notes: 2024 items from Enduro21 first look (Husqvarna data); 2025 items and feel from Dirt Bike Magazine test.

records.statement: Husqvarna did not offer the FX 450 for 2026 (only the FX 350, with AT82 tyres, a threaded radiator cap and a fuel-line cap); the FX 450 returned for 2027.

source.name: Enduro21: Quick Look 2027 Husqvarna cross-country range - FX 450 returns

records.notes: Dirt Bike Magazine 2026 Husqvarna line-up also lists only the FX 350.

records.statement: The 2023 Husqvarna FE 450 returned after three years as the off-road competition enduro, based on the FC 450 with a 12.75:1 engine, 42 mm throttle body, Pankl 6-speed with per-gear mapping, two maps plus traction control, a 2.4 gal tank and a claimed 251 lb curb weight. It uses a linkage WP XACT shock, not KTM's PDS.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling: 2023 Husqvarna FE 450 First Look

records.notes: Husqvarna data via Ultimate Motorcycling first look.

records.statement: The 2024 FE 450 got the new chromoly frame and hybrid subframe, a WP XACT closed-cartridge fork replacing the XPLOR fork, a linkage XACT shock, Braktec brakes and clutch, a fuse-less off-road control unit and pegs with 27% more area set 3 mm lower. Claimed weight 109.8 kg without fuel with an 8 L tank. 2025 MSRP $12,249.

source.name: MotoOnline: Tested 2024 Husqvarna FE range

records.notes: Australian launch data; US price from Cycle World 2025 XCF-W page competitor list.

records.topic: GasGas EX first generation vs KTM
records.statement: The first GasGas EX four-strokes (2021) used the KTM XC-F engine, frame, suspension, wheels and brakes but with forged instead of billet triple clamps, a softer rounder seat, no resonance chamber on the mid-pipe, no hour meter, no map switch fitted and a lower price ($9,999 vs $10,699 for the KTM 350 XC-F).

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country

records.notes: Magazine test. 2023 EX models are assumed to keep this generation (GasGas's 2024 range brought the new frame); not separately confirmed.

records.topic: GasGas EX 2024 changes and differences from MC
records.statement: For 2024 the GasGas EX got the new frame with an aluminium subframe (KTM/Husqvarna use polyamide hybrids), Braktec brakes, a 9 L tank (+0.5 L) with integrated pump, an 18-inch rear wheel, sidestand, off-road race mapping and a WP XACT closed-cartridge spring fork where the MC has an air fork. The map switch (2 maps, traction control, quickshifter) is an optional accessory, unlike the standard switch on the KTM XC-F.

source.name: GasGas Canada: 2024 EX 450F model page

records.notes: Combined from GasGas Canada page and Vital MX launch report.

records.topic: GasGas EX and EC 450F dropped for 2026
records.statement: GasGas dropped the EX 250F, EX 350F, EX 450F and EC 450F for 2026; the EX 300 two-stroke was its only cross-country model, and enduro four-strokes were the EC 350F and EC 500F.

source.name: Enduro21: First look 2026 GasGas off-road range

records.notes: Cycle News 2026 GasGas specs article also lists only the EX 300 cross-country model.

records.statement: The GasGas EC 450F (US from October 2023) is the GasGas version of the KTM 450 XCF-W and Husqvarna FE 450: 12.75:1 compression, 42 mm throttle body, Pankl 6-speed with a map per gear, a WP XPLOR open-cartridge fork and linkage WP XACT shock, a 2.4 gal tank and an LED headlight. Claimed 244 lb without fuel; MSRP $11,399.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2024 GasGas Enduro Bikes First Look

records.notes: GasGas data via Dirt Rider first look.

records.statement: The 450 XC-F engine is the SX-F SOHC unit: 95 x 63.4 mm, 13.1:1 compression, 44 mm Keihin throttle body, 40 mm intake and 33 mm exhaust valves with DLC-coated rocker arms; KTM quotes 59 lb engine weight.

source.name: KTM 2024 450 XC-F model page

records.notes: 13.1:1 also in Dirt Rider 2023/2025 data.

records.statement: The enduro 450s (KTM 450 XCF-W, Husqvarna FE 450, GasGas EC 450F) run 12.75:1 compression and a 42 mm throttle body, against 13.1:1 and 44 mm on the 450 XC-F/FX 450/EX 450F, and use a wide-ratio 6-speed instead of the XC-F's 5-speed.

source.name: Cycle World: 2025 KTM 450 XCF-W

records.notes: Cycle World (KTM data) for XCF-W; Husqvarna/GasGas figures from Ultimate Motorcycling and Dirt Rider first looks. Dirt Bike Magazine said the 2023 XCF-W shared the 2022 450 XC-F compression and valve sizes, which disagrees with the 12.75:1 figure.

records.statement: KTM lists the 350 XC-F at 88 x 57.5 mm, DOHC, 14.6:1, and the 250 XC-F at 81 x 48.5 mm, DOHC, 14.5:1.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling: 2024 KTM Cross Country Lineup First Look

records.notes: The article labels the 250 lines '250 SX-F' (likely a copy error). Dirt Rider listed the 2022 350 XC-F at 14.2:1 (previous generation).

records.statement: The 450 XCF-W intake boot has no reed valve (the EXC-F and old XCF-W used one) and the evaporative system is gone. KTM fits a two-piece header close to the engine and a short aluminium silencer with spark arrestor; the bike is much quieter than the competition models and gives up some power to the exhaust. The 2026 airbox adds an enduro splash protector underneath.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2023 KTM 450XCF-W Full Test

records.notes: Combined from Dirt Bike Magazine 2023 test, Cycle News 2023 announcement and KTM 2026 page. No dB figure found.

records.statement: Early GasGas EX four-strokes use a straight-tube header with no resonance chamber, where the KTM uses a resonance-chamber header; testers count this as one reason the EX made less peak power.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2021 GasGas EX 250F Dyno Test

records.notes: MXA 2021 EX 350F test also notes no resonance chamber on the mid-pipe.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2023 450 XC-F made 54.6 hp at 9,500 rpm and 33.0 lb-ft at 7,000 rpm. That is 2.5 hp more and 0.8 lb-ft less than the 2019 model.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2023 KTM 450 XC-F Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. Compare only with other Dirt Rider Dynojet numbers.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2025 450 XC-F made 54.2 hp and 33.6 lb-ft.

source.name: Dirt Rider: How Much Power Does the 2025 KTM 450 XC-F Make?

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. Rpm points not stated.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2023 450 XCF-W made 48.3 hp at 9,200 rpm and 31.9 lb-ft at 7,400 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2023 KTM 450 XCF-W Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. Dunlop D404 street tyre on the rear. 2023 XCF-W is the old-frame model; tester praised delivery over peak numbers.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2023 250 XC-F made 40.5 hp at 13,000 rpm and 19.0 lb-ft at 9,800 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2023 KTM 250 XC-F Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2022 350 XC-F made 50.3 hp at 12,000 rpm and 26.8 lb-ft at 8,600 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2022 KTM 350 XC-F Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house dyno (model not named in this article, Dynojet 250i in others), Dunlop D404 street tyre, stock. Said to equal the 2022 RM-Z450 peak.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2020 Husqvarna FX 350 made 49.1 hp at 11,700 rpm and 25.5 lb-ft at 8,700 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2020 Husqvarna FX 350 Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2023 Husqvarna FX 350 made 50.9 hp at 11,400 rpm and 26.8 lb-ft at 8,800 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: How Much Power Does the 2023 Husqvarna FX 350 Make?

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2025 Husqvarna FX 350 made 51.0 hp and 27.0 lb-ft.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2025 Husqvarna FX 350 Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. Rpm points not stated. Tester called it closer to a mellow 450 than a 250F.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2020 Husqvarna FX 450 made 51.1 hp at 10,000 rpm and 32.2 lb-ft at 7,600 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2020 Husqvarna FX 450 Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2021 Husqvarna FX 450 made 51.5 hp at 9,300 rpm and 32.9 lb-ft at 7,300 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2021 Husqvarna FX 450 Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. D404 street tyre.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2023 Husqvarna FX 450 made 53.3 hp at 10,400 rpm and 32.2 lb-ft at 7,500 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: How Much Power Does the 2023 Husqvarna FX 450 Make?

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. Tester described linear, controllable delivery.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2021 GasGas EX 350F made 48.9 hp at 11,800 rpm and 25.3 lb-ft at 8,800 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2021 GasGas EX 350F Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. D404 street tyre; 0.2 hp and 0.2 lb-ft below the 2020 FX 350 per the article.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2021 GasGas EX 250F made 39.3 hp at 13,300 rpm and 18.8 lb-ft at 9,200 rpm. Power and torque dipped clearly between 4,300 and 4,700 rpm on every pull, then rose steeply from 5,300 rpm and stayed linear. It made 1.8 hp less than the 2021 250 SX-F, blamed on no vented airbox cover, no map 2 and the straight header.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2021 GasGas EX 250F Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. No map switch fitted, so map 1 only.

records.statement: On a magazine rear-wheel dyno the 2024 GasGas EX 250F made 41.9 hp and 20.0 lb-ft. The tester described long, linear power with no hard hit that still revs out, which suits the wide-ratio 6-speed.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2024 GasGas EX 250F Dyno Test

records.notes: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i, stock bike, fuel and map not stated. Rpm points not stated.

records.statement: Worked out from the same magazine dyno, the 2023 450 XCF-W made 6.3 hp (about 12%) and 1.1 lb-ft less than the 2023 450 XC-F, with peak power 300 rpm lower.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2023 KTM 450 XCF-W Dyno Test

records.notes: 48.3 - 54.6 = -6.3 hp; -6.3/54.6 = -11.5%. 31.9 - 33.0 = -1.1 lb-ft; -1.1/33.0 = -3.3%. 9,200 - 9,500 = -300 rpm. Both Dirt Rider Dynojet 250i 2023; the 2023 XCF-W is the old-generation engine/chassis, so part of the gap may be generation, not just intake/exhaust/map.

records.statement: Worked out from the same magazine dyno, the 2023 FX 350 made only 2.4 hp less peak power than the FX 450 but 5.4 lb-ft (17%) less torque, peaking 1,000 rpm higher. That matches testers saying the 350 is about 3 hp short of a 450 but needs revs.

source.name: Dirt Rider: How Much Power Does the 2023 Husqvarna FX 350 Make?

records.statement: Worked out from the same magazine dyno, the 2023 FX 450 made 1.3 hp and 0.8 lb-ft less than the 2023 450 XC-F and peaked 900 rpm higher, despite sharing the engine; the difference is within what unit-to-unit and airbox/exhaust differences can produce.

source.name: Dirt Rider: How Much Power Does the 2023 Husqvarna FX 450 Make?

records.notes: 53.3-54.6 = -1.3; 32.2-33.0 = -0.8; 10,400-9,500 = +900. Single samples; do not treat as a brand difference.

records.statement: Testers call the 450 XCF-W the smoothest KTM four-stroke from bottom to top, with no coughing or decel popping; it lugs to very low rpm and finds traction where a motocross bike spins. Peak power sits between the dual-sport and the XC-F.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2023 KTM 450XCF-W Full Test

records.notes: Tester impression, stock bike. Dirt Rider dyno tester likewise said it builds from the lowest rpm and never feels like too much.

records.statement: On the 2024 XCF-W low rpm is tame, the midrange ramps up strongly and it revs to about 11,000 rpm; torque lets you hold a high gear without bogging. Map 2 is sharp but not abrupt and suits skilled riders.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling: 2024 KTM 450 XCF-W Review (GNCC tested)

records.notes: Tester impression with optional map switch fitted, GNCC-style course.

records.statement: Testers say the 450 XC-F has as much peak power as any production 450 yet stays manageable, but it stalls more easily than the 350 in tight going and the spinning mass makes it more work at low speed.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: Riding the 2025 KTM 450XC-F (The Wrap)

records.notes: Tester impression, stock.

records.statement: Testers describe strong bottom-end pull, a good midrange and more pull on top; it can be ridden like a 450 but rewards revving. In slow, rocky, technical sections the throttle response felt jerky.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2025 KTM 350 XC-F review

records.notes: 185 lb tester, stock engine, both maps tried.

records.statement: The FX 350 is only about 3 hp short of a 450, pulls a long way, and can be short-shifted when tired; off-road it is ridden lower in the rpm than on a motocross track (mostly under 9,000 rpm), and it stalls less than a 450.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2025 Husqvarna FX350 Full Test

records.notes: Tester impression.

records.statement: The EX bikes keep the motocross engine character: free-revving with strong mid-to-top pull, but less bottom-end tractability and a less smooth throttle off idle than the EC enduro models.

source.name: Transmoto: 2024 GasGas Cross-Country Weapons

records.notes: Tester comparison at the 2024 launch.

records.statement: The 2024 FE 450 is smooth and easy to ride with strong low-end grunt and good climbing, pulling from corners in 2nd-4th; it feels heavier and needs more effort in tight sections than the FE 250/350 and sometimes pushed the front.

source.name: ADB Magazine: Enduro Test 2024 Husqvarna FE 450

records.notes: Australian enduro test; MotoOnline launch report agrees on weight in slow sections.

records.statement: The 2021 EX 350F felt weaker than the 350 SX-F and would not pull 3rd cleanly out of a tight uphill turn; testers traced it to the airbox, not the engine.

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country

records.notes: Tester impression; see engine_mods for the airbox fix.

records.topic: XC-F map switch, traction and launch control
records.statement: The XC-F has a standard bar switch with two maps (Map 1 more linear, Map 2 sharper throttle response) and a traction control toggle. Launch control is engaged by pressing the traction control and quickshift buttons together, and the quickshifter works 2nd-5th on the 450 (2nd-6th on the 250/350).

source.name: KTM 2024 450 XC-F model page

records.notes: QS ranges from MXA 2024 first look. Map lights: white = map 1, green = map 2.

records.statement: KTM-group traction control has no wheel-speed sensor. It compares throttle input with how fast engine rpm rises and cuts power when rpm climbs too quickly. It still allows deliberate slides on consistent ground and mainly steps in on slick rock or wet clay; it works with either map, giving four combinations, and keeps its setting after a stall.

source.name: KTM USA 2026 450 XCF-W model page

records.notes: Mechanism from the KTM 2026 XCF-W page; behaviour and orange TC light from Transmoto 2017 test of the same system.

records.statement: On the 450 XCF-W the map switch, traction control and quickshifter (2nd-6th) are optional, unlocked by a PowerParts switch expected to cost under $200; they are standard on the XC-F. The map light is hard to see in direct sun and the TC and QS buttons sit close together.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling: 2024 KTM 450 XCF-W Review (GNCC tested)

records.notes: KTM 2026 page confirms the switch is optional.

records.statement: GasGas EX bikes ship without the map switch: the stock map matches Map 1 of the KTM SX-F, and Map 2, traction control, launch control and (from 2024) the quickshifter are in the ECU but need the plug-in switch ($160 in 2021).

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country

records.notes: GasGas 2024 EX 450F page confirms the switch is an optional accessory.

records.statement: The enduro 450s (and the GasGas EX 450F per GasGas) use a gear-position sensor on the shift drum so the ECU runs a separate map in each gear.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2024 GasGas Enduro Bikes First Look

records.notes: Husqvarna FE 450 per-gear mapping from Ultimate Motorcycling 2023 first look.

records.statement: 2023 six-speed XC-F and FX 350 owners can get the quickshifter by a dealer software update.

source.name: Motocross Action: First Look 2024 KTM off-road models

records.notes: Enduro21 2024 Husqvarna first look confirms for FX 350.

records.statement: The Connectivity Unit Offroad bolts behind the number plate with a GPS sensor in the front fender and pairs with the KTMconnect app. It can retrofit 2024-2025 XC-F bikes (standard on 350 XC-F Factory Edition) and adjusts engine braking, throttle response, traction control, launch control and quickshifter, with presets for sand, gravel, hard pack, dry and wet. The rider subscription is 69.99 euro a year; testers put the hardware at about $250.

source.name: KTM tech guide: Connectivity Unit Offroad

records.notes: Hardware price from Dirt Bike Magazine 2025 450 XC-F test. KTM does not list the XCF-W as compatible. Numeric parameter ranges not published.

records.topic: traction control stalling on soft map
records.statement: One tester found that running the softer map with traction control on in tight single track caused repeated coughing and stalling; turning traction control off helped but did not cure the slow-speed throttle response.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2025 KTM 350 XC-F review

records.notes: Single tester report.

records.statement: A vented KTM airbox cover (winglet removed) noticeably improved pull out of tight uphill turns on the EX 350F, and with no cover it pulled 3rd cleanly; testers concluded the stock EX airbox starves the engine of air.

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country

records.notes: Back-to-back seat-of-pants test, no dyno numbers. No-cover running suggested only for dry, non-race use.

records.statement: Testers say an aftermarket exhaust recovers about half of the extra power racers want from the XCF-W; remapping and cam changes make up the rest.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2023 KTM 450XCF-W Full Test

records.notes: Qualitative; no dyno numbers given.

records.statement: The 450 XC-F and FX 450 cases accept a sixth gear: OEM parts (6th gear pair, shift drum) cost about $300 and the job takes about 3 hours with the engine out and cases split. Desert racers fit it, often with 14/48 sprockets, because the 5-speed runs out of gear on fast terrain.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test: Tech Tip - KTM 450 XC-F 6th gear install

records.notes: Dirt Bike Magazine 2025 test says many desert racers install the six-speed gearbox from the 500 XC-W. Top speed after the swap not measured.

records.statement: Riders who use the clutch heavily in tight single track can overheat it; testers suggest an auto-clutch, a lower gearing or a smoother low-speed map.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2025 KTM 350 XC-F review

records.notes: Dirt Bike Magazine 2025 450 XC-F test also warns intermediate riders can overheat the clutch.

records.statement: The 450 XC-F and FX 450 use the same 5-speed as the SX-F/FC 450; the 250 and 350 XC-F/FX/EX use a 6-speed (the SX-F/FC/MC 250 and 350 have 5). For 2023 KTM kept the 2022 XC ratios: a semi-close set with an added 6th, not the wide enduro set.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test: Inside scoop on 2023 KTMs

records.notes: Vital MX 2024 GasGas report says the EX 450F also uses the MC 5-speed; see conflicts.

records.statement: The 450 XCF-W uses a wide-ratio 6-speed shared with the 500 EXC-F, which testers found useful in every gear; primary 29:72, final 13:52.

source.name: Cycle News: New 2024 KTM 450 XCF-W Four-Stroke Model Specs

records.notes: Gearbox sharing from Dirt Bike Magazine 2023 test.

records.statement: Compared with the MX 5-speed, the EX 350F 6-speed has a much lower 1st, slightly taller 2nd and noticeably taller 3rd-5th; 6th is unusable on an MX track. Stock gearing is 14/51; testers used 14/52 or 13/50 for MX to make 3rd usable.

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country

records.statement: Stock 350 XC-F gearing is 14/50. A 14/51 rear pulled 3rd better through corners and eased clutch use but made 2nd feel too short and the throttle more on/off, so the tester went back to stock.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2025 KTM 350 XC-F review

records.notes: Single tester, 185 lb.

records.statement: Testers felt the 2023-2024 XC-F frame was too rigid; the 2025 frame with cut-outs is more compliant and rides better almost everywhere.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: Riding the 2025 KTM 450XC-F (The Wrap)

records.notes: Dirt Bike Magazine 2025 FX350 test says the same of the Husqvarna 2025 frame (no break-in needed).

records.topic: measured seat height FX 450 vs 450 XC-F
records.statement: Measured by the same magazine, the 2023 FX 450 seat was 37.2 in against 37.8 in on the 2023 450 XC-F, so the Husqvarna sits about 0.6 in (15 mm) lower.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2023 Husqvarna FX 450 Technical Information

records.notes: 37.8-37.2 = 0.6 in x 25.4 = 15 mm. Both Dirt Rider measured 2023. Husqvarna lowers the FC/FX through suspension settings.

records.statement: The XCF-W's linkless PDS shock gives more ground clearance and nothing to snag on logs and rocks. With the soft 2023 setup the bike felt pitchy and divey at high speed and was happiest under 30-40 mph.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2023 KTM 450XCF-W Full Test

records.notes: Cycle World also cites the snag-free PDS benefit.

records.statement: Testers fixed front-end push on the GasGas by torquing the top triple clamp bolts to 20 Nm and the bottom to 15 Nm, the figures they got from KTM's test department, instead of the 17/12 Nm they had been using.

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country

records.notes: Source writes N/mm, read here as Nm torque.

records.statement: From 2024 the cross-country XC-F, FX and EX use a WP XACT closed-cartridge spring fork with a linkage XACT shock (300 mm each end). The enduro 450s differ: the KTM 450 XCF-W pairs the XACT closed-cartridge fork with a linkless WP XPLOR PDS shock (310 mm), the Husqvarna FE 450 uses the XACT fork with a linkage shock, and the GasGas EC 450F uses a WP XPLOR open-cartridge fork with a linkage XACT shock. Before 2024 the XC-F/FX/EX ran the XACT air fork (310 mm).

source.name: Transmoto: 2024 GasGas Cross-Country Weapons

records.notes: Compiled from KTM, GasGas, Husqvarna press data (Cycle World, Dirt Rider, MotoOnline, Transmoto).

records.statement: The XC-F shock has the same spring as the SX-F but is valved softer, like a soft MX setting; it suits WORCS-style racing but is too stiff in desert rock fields, and the fork is slightly stiff picking through boulders in 1st.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: Riding the 2025 KTM 450XC-F (The Wrap)

records.notes: Tester impression.

records.topic: XACT spring fork vs XPLOR on the trail
records.statement: Testers find the XACT closed-cartridge fork racier: it handles big hits, braking bumps and ruts well but is harsher on roots and loose rock than the EC's XPLOR fork, which in turn is too soft on big hits. The FE 450's switch from XPLOR to XACT made it firmer and less prone to bottoming.

source.name: Transmoto: 2024 GasGas Cross-Country Weapons

records.notes: ADB 2024 EX 350F and FE 450 tests agree.

records.statement: The 2023 XCF-W's XPLOR fork was softer than a motocross setup and may be too soft even for hard trail riders; the 2024 XACT closed-cartridge fork was seen as a big improvement.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2023 KTM 450XCF-W Full Test

records.notes: Cycle World calls the 2024 fork change 'a major improvement'.

records.topic: 350 XC-F tester setup (185 lb, vet B)
records.statement: A 185 lb vet tester ran the fork 5 clicks out compression, 12 out rebound, tubes at the second line, and the shock at 11 out low-speed compression, 1 turn out high-speed, 12 out rebound with 105 mm sag on stock 14/50 gearing and the green map. For fast desert he suggests dropping the fork to the first line or flush.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2025 KTM 350 XC-F review

records.notes: Stock springs; tester notes bigger/faster riders need a shock spring and revalve.

records.statement: A magazine MX/cross-country setup for the air-fork EX 350F: 9.8 bar (142 psi), 12 out compression, 18 out rebound, tubes at the second line; shock 42 N/mm spring (45 N/mm over 185 lb), 105 mm sag, high-speed 1.5 turns out (stock 2), low-speed 15 out, rebound 15 out.

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country

records.notes: Applies to air-fork years (2021-2023). Check air daily and bleed the fork.

records.statement: A 160 lb tester raced the 2024 XCF-W on stock suspension (sag correct out of the box) with Map 2 and traction control off on the open grass sections, and recommends Map 1 for technical woods.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling: 2024 KTM 450 XCF-W Review (GNCC tested)

records.notes: Dunlop MX33/AT81 stock tyres.

records.topic: Vegas to Reno 450 XC-F desert build
records.statement: A desert race team ran a 450 XC-F with an added 6th gear, 14/48 gearing (stock 13T front), an FMF slip-on for more bottom-to-mid, a 3.2 gal tank (about 70 fast miles per tank), revalved suspension, 100-110 mm sag and fork air at 135-141 psi.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test: Inside the race bike - Vegas to Reno KTM 450XC-F (3Bros Racing)

records.notes: The bike was a 2019, the same generation as 2020-2022.

records.statement: Stock settings suit most vet tracks; on faster tracks add at least a few clicks of fork compression, and the rear is usually fine.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: 2025 Husqvarna FX350 Full Test

records.statement: The stock soft setting suits WORCS-style racing; desert racers need firmer settings for rocks, and many add a 6th gear because the 5-speed is the bike's main shortcoming for western racing.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: Riding the 2025 KTM 450XC-F (The Wrap)

records.statement: In August 2026 KTM North America recalled about 21,040 Husqvarna and GasGas off-road bikes in the US (plus about 4,140 in Canada) because the rear brake caliper can crack or break. In this slice it covers the 2023 FX 350, FX 450 and FE 450, the 2023-2024 GasGas EX 250F/350F/450F and the 2024 EC 450F. Stop riding and get the free dealer repair. KTM-brand models are not on the list.

source.name: US CPSC recall 26-710: KTM North America recalls off-road motorcycles (rear brake caliper)

records.notes: 2024 Husqvarna FX and FE 450 are not listed (2024 FE 350w/501w are). No incidents reported.

records.statement: Some owners report the fuel pump fuse blowing or the pump dying (one at 70 hours), sometimes after long idling with little fuel. Owners fixed it by replacing the pump and fuel filter and keeping enough fuel to cover the pump.

source.name: Vital MX forum: 2023 KTM 250 XC-F fuel pump failure? Is this common?

records.notes: Few reports; others in the thread had no issues. Not a bulletin.

records.topic: 450 runs out of gear in the desert
records.statement: The 5-speed 450 XC-F/FX 450 runs out of gear on dry lakes and fast desert; a 6th gear or taller gearing is the usual fix, and testers say a 6-speed 350 XC-F can be faster at the top.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test: Tech Tip - KTM 450 XC-F 6th gear install

records.notes: Top-speed claim not measured.

records.statement: Clutch-heavy riders can overheat the clutch in tight single track; one tester boiled coolant twice on a 350 XC-F.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2025 KTM 350 XC-F review

records.notes: Dirt Bike Magazine 2025 450 XC-F test gives the same warning.

records.statement: Testers found the rim-lock spoke loosens quickly, the plastic shock preload ring gets chewed up, the bayonet fuel cap clogs with dirt, and the fork bleed screws are Torx.

source.name: Motocross Action: Race Test of the 2021 GasGas EX 350F cross-country
